principle: Every HTML element must be tagged with its source IDs. This is critical for the Inspector. No image or video may exist without a data-des attribute.

attribute_rules.data-edt: on <section> elements — from editor.json section IDs.

attribute_rules.data-des: on EVERY visual element — charts, images, videos, interactives, stat callouts. No image or video may exist without it.

attribute_rules.data-cin: on each cinematic-background SCENE element — the cin_xx scene id. The cinematic scroll background is a MANDATORY stage on every blog, so data-cin is emitted for EVERY scene under ANY on-mode (photographic/generative/data_driven); do NOT gate it on 'cinematic' (that value is only a retired backward-compat alias for photographic). It sits ALONGSIDE the background's data-sct/data-des (an image/video scene's background carries its verified-source tag via the scene's media_ref; a data_driven chart-spine/gradient scene has no media_ref), so both the scene and, where present, its licensed source are traceable. validate.py §6b ERRORs cinematic_data_driven_not_built when mode is data_driven but no data-cin is on the page.
attribute_rules.data-int: on the ROOT of EVERY interactive playground (only when interaction.json exists) — the hero centerpiece AND every supporting[] playground — the int_xx id. It sits ALONGSIDE data-des and data-ana, so the centerpiece + each supporting interactive is traceable to interaction.json (centerpiece/supporting[]) and gets a verify_map entry. validate.py resolves the hero from interaction.centerpiece.id and each supporting id from interaction.supporting[].id — a data-int with no matching id is a dangling tag.
attribute_rules.data-play-out: NON-PROVENANCE hook, NOT a provenance prefix — optional, on a playground's live readout element, value = its int_xx id (e.g. data-play-out="int_02"). It is NOT validated and NOT in any data-* tuple/schema (like data-backs); it only lets the Playtester read a chart-only readout change the coarse innerText diff would miss. Never use it in place of data-int.
attribute_rules.chart_id: Every chart container's id attribute should be the des_xx ID.
attribute_rules.editorial_paragraphs: Paragraphs tagged [editorial] in editor.md get no data-ana — they are connective prose.
attribute_rules.multi_id_format: Multiple IDs of the same kind go in ONE data-* attribute, comma-separated with NO spaces (e.g. data-det="det_02,det_05"). validate.py splits the value on commas, so a space-separated value (data-det="det_02 det_05") becomes a single token and is flagged as a dangling tag. Different kinds keep their own attributes (data-ana="..." data-det="..."). Connective [editorial] paragraphs carry no data-ana/data-det.

example: <!-- Section container — data-edt on section, data-det for detective context -->
<section data-edt="edt_01" data-det="det_02,det_05">
Section Title
<!-- editor.md says: [ana_01] 20.1% of people chose the Ace of Spades... -->
20.1% of people chose the Ace of Spades...
<!-- editor.md says: [ana_04, det_02] The second most popular choice... -->
The second most popular choice...
<!-- editor.md says: [editorial] This pattern reveals something deeper... -->
This pattern reveals something deeper...
<!-- Chart — tagged with designer ID and data source -->
</section>
<!-- EVERY image must have data-des — no exceptions -->
<!-- Scout-sourced image: ALSO carries data-sct (its designer item has media_ref: sct_03) -->
<!-- EVERY video must have data-des — no exceptions -->
<video data-des="des_02" autoplay loop muted playsinline><source src="assets/teaser_hero.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
<!-- Stat callout — tagged with designer ID and data source -->
20.1%chose the Ace of Spades
